skeleton.finalText:
I've written `src/server.ts`, and `npm run build` finishes with no errors. I started the server and sent it a request: `POST /requisitions.csv` came back as `501 Not Implemented` with an empty body.

- **Server:** it listens on `Number(process.env.PORT)` at `process.env.HOST ?? "127.0.0.1"` and answers every request with 501 and an empty body. It has no routing, logic or helpers.
- **Route docs:** there are three doc comments. The main one covers `POST /requisitions.csv`: the JSON array body, the 200 CSV answer with its headers and layout, the quoting and formula rules, the 422 and the 400. The other two cover 405 with `Allow: POST` for other methods on that path, and 404 for other paths. All of it uses the spec's wording.
- **Exported types:**
  - `RequisitionStatus`
  - `Requisition`, where `title?: string | null`
  - `RequisitionsCsvRequest`, which is `Requisition[]`
  - `UnprocessableRequisitionError`, which is `{ error, id }`
  - `BadRequestError`, which is `{ error }`

  Nothing else is exported. The spec doesn't define a body for the 405 or 404, so neither has a type.
- **Test-controlled inputs:** none are needed. The behaviour doesn't depend on the clock, a secret or randomness; the only time involved is each requisition's `createdAt`, which comes in the request.

The build compiled a `src/server.js`; I deleted it so that `src/server.ts` is the only file I've added. No other files were touched.

I deleted `tests/public/helpers.ts` and its compiled `helpers.js`. The only source files in `tests/public/` now are the four `*.test.ts` files.

- **What changed:** each test file now has its own copy of the helpers it uses: the requisition builder, the POST helpers and `assertCsv`. Only `refusals.test.ts` also has `assertJsonError`, since it's the only file that checks error answers. The tests are the same as before.
- **Build:** `npm run build` reports no errors.
- **Suite run:** `node sandbox/boundary.mjs -- node sandbox/run.mjs public` gives `public: 0/36 passed`. Every failure is the stub's 501 status, as expected.
- **Check against the reference:** I ran the rewritten files against the throwaway reference server in the scratchpad again, and all 36 passed.

That reference server is still listening on port 47811, because the sandbox won't let me stop it. Please run `kill $(lsof -ti tcp:47811)` to stop it.

private.finalText:
I wrote the private suite in `tests/private/`. All 48 tests fail against the current 501 stub, and `npm run build` reports no errors.

**Checking it.** The public suite has no implementation to run against, so I wrote a throwaway reference implementation in the scratchpad. It's not in the project. All 36 public tests and all 48 private tests pass against it. I then made 13 shortcut versions of it. 11 pass the public suite and fail the private one; the other two (sorting by id alone, and quoting before defusing) already fail public tests, and fail more private ones. The shortcuts:
- sorting by id alone, or by UTC date then id
- comparing times only to the millisecond
- writing numbers with `String(n)`, which gives `1e+21`
- quoting any field that starts or ends with any whitespace, not just a space
- treating an empty id `""` as missing
- ignoring the minutes of an offset (`+05:30`)
- treating every year divisible by 4 as a leap year
- answering 405 only for GET/PUT/PATCH/DELETE
- matching paths with `endsWith`
- trimming spaces off times or accepting `+002026` years
- checking every item's status before any other field, so the wrong bad requisition gets named
- quoting the title before defusing it

**Two choices that rest on a strict reading of the spec:**
- **Sub-millisecond times:** two times that differ only below a millisecond are ordered by time, not by id. An implementation built on `Date.parse` fails this.
- **Tabs:** a title ending in a tab is not quoted, because the spec says "a space", not any whitespace.

**Files:** the four files match the public ones (`layout`, `quoting`, `formula`, `refusals`). Each test's name starts with its scenario key, and a comment above it names the public test it extends.

**Left out because the spec leaves them open:** leap second `:60`, hour `24:00:00`, offsets above `+23:59`, lowercase `t`/`z`, comparing ids with different letter case, a query string on the path, the request's Content-Type, extra fields on a requisition, and which status wins when a body has both a 400 item and a 422 item.

48 tests, in 4 files.

Open in the spec:
The spec gives the error body as `{"error": <a message>}` (400) or `{"error": ..., "id": ...}` (422). It doesn't say whether other keys may also appear. Each public test below requires exactly those keys; my tests only check that `error` is a string and `id` matches.
- `[unhappy-2] a requisition with an unknown status is refused with 422 naming its id`
- `[unhappy-2] statuses written as in the CSV, or missing, are unknown`
- `[unhappy-2] a title that is neither a string nor null is refused`
- `[unhappy-2] openings or filled that is not a whole number of at least 0 is refused`
- `[unhappy-2] filled one more than openings is refused, filled equal to openings is not`
- `[unhappy-2] a creation time not written as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS with Z or an offset is refused`
- `[unhappy-2] a creation time that names no real time is refused`
- `[unhappy-2] when several requisitions are bad, the first in the request's order is named`
- `[unhappy-3] a body that is not JSON is refused with 400`
- `[unhappy-3] an empty body or plain text is not JSON`
- `[unhappy-3] JSON that is not an array is refused with 400`
- `[unhappy-3] an item that is not an object with a string id is refused with 400`
